g.text: Set once and left alone. The session goes on being measured underneath.
Where Zerg looks for the event files (.jsonl) the VibeXI addon writes. It follows
the newest one in the folder. Change this only if the addon writes somewhere
3 event files in this folder; the newest is Hasaya-20261005203112.jsonl.
The keys that switch every floating panel between click-through and clickable,
from any application, the game included. Click the keys, then press the new
ones: Ctrl, Alt or Win held with a letter, a digit or F1 to F24.
Waiting for the new keys. Esc cancels.
How solid the dark backdrop of a pop-out is; its text and bars stay solid. Every
pop-out follows this until the slider on its own bar is moved. From then on that
pop-out keeps its own opacity, whatever is set here.
How many times a second everything that moves with the clock is redrawn: the
elapsed time, every DPS and HPS figure, and the right-hand edge of the
Cumulative damage and Cumulative healing charts. Whatever an event changes
is redrawn as soon as the event arrives. Higher is smoother and uses more
A share can be drawn as the row itself, shaded from its left edge to the length of
the share. A row that is not shaded shows its share as a small bar in its Damage
%, Healing % or Share cell instead. The pop-outs follow both switches.
A character’s row in Damage by character and Healing by
character, their heading in Actions and Heals, and the two runs in
The rows under a character, shaded without a colour.
Accuracy, WS Acc and Pet Acc under this are marked in red, more strongly the
lower they fall: a rule under the figure first, then the cell cut out. At 60% and
under the mark is at its strongest.
Light, dark, or whatever Windows is set to.
The colour of each run in Compare: its band across a row, its badge, and its
columns and lines in the charts. Any colour can be picked. Zerg works out how
strong the band is from the colour, so figures and changes stay readable on it.
as set; the bands come out at 20% and 19%
